raw_response:
My reasoning:

I have 7.5 mu to manage. Like most years, I put the main field in wheat-maize rotation — that is 5 mu, two crops on the same ground. The other 2.5 mu is vegetable land near the house where water is easy from the well. I split it: 1 mu cabbage in autumn, 0.8 mu chili in spring, 0.7 mu eggplant in spring.

For wheat, I do what I did last year — it gave me over 450 kg last season so I keep the same way. I use improved variety seed from the town agricultural station, about 15 kg per mu. Before sowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer 15-15-15, that is 50 kg per mu as base, then top-dress 15 kg urea at jointing. That works out to about 16 kg N, 7-8 kg P, 7-8 kg K. I plough once in autumn before sowing wheat. Water 3 times — once after sowing, once at jointing in spring, once at filling. Spray twice for aphids and wheat midge.

For maize after wheat harvest, no time to plough, I just rotary-till and plant hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu. Base fertilizer one bag compound 15-15-15, then top-dress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. Maize needs water — I give 2 waterings from the well if rain is short. Spray once for corn borer.

Vegetables need more fertilizer and more spray, everyone knows this. Cabbage I plant end of July, needs heavy manure and nitrogen for big heads. Chili and eggplant sit in the field from April to September, many sprays needed because of pests. I use hybrid seed for all three — vegetables without hybrid seed do not sell well at market.
